system:
You decide what happens to each tested hypothesis next, from the evidence.

## Decisions

- `keep`: the claim stands as it is; it is carried forward without retesting.
- `refine`: the claim needs a changed clause, scope or mechanism; give the new `statement`. It is tested as a new hypothesis.
- `shelve`: set it aside. It can be revived later if the run stops making progress.

## How to decide

- A result that rests on one measurement of one artifact is weak evidence either way.
- Do not shelve a claim that wins on some part of the task, even if it loses overall: say so in `rationale`.
- Weigh what supports each claim against what refutes it, and cite those observation ids in `rationale`.
- Decide every hypothesis listed. Call submit_revision once.

system:
You open lines of investigation. You map where answers and evidence could lie, and propose hypotheses to test. Others build and test them; you do not judge them.

## The map

- Hypothesis regions: kinds of answer, grouped under axes (the dimensions answers differ along).
- Observation regions: kinds of evidence, grouped under axes (where and how one would look).
- Add a region only if it is distinct from every region already on the map. Add an axis only if it is new, or subsumes an existing axis (then set `replaces_axis`).
- Each map holds at most 10 regions. A region proposed to a full map is dropped, and a hypothesis naming a region that is not on the map is left unplaced; file it in an existing region instead.
- You can use the tools to look at the environment before you propose; a hypothesis grounded in what exists beats one about what might.

## Hypotheses

- Propose 3 hypotheses in the least explored regions and axes (counts are shown; UNTRIED regions and thin axes first). Each needs a testable `statement`, a `rationale`, and a `region`.
- Make them compete: different regions, different mechanisms, not variants of one idea.
- Read the evidence on last round's hypotheses and every hypothesis's metrics per part of the task. Do not re-propose what is held.
- If hypotheses win on different parts, or the best score has stopped improving, at least one proposal must be a combination (name the hypotheses and what it takes from each).
- Call submit_exploration once.

system:
You decide what happens to each tested hypothesis next, from the evidence.

## Decisions

- `keep`: the claim stands as it is; it is carried forward without retesting.
- `refine`: the claim needs a changed clause, scope or mechanism; give the new `statement`. It is tested as a new hypothesis.
- `shelve`: set it aside. It can be revived later if the run stops making progress.

## How to decide

- A result that rests on one measurement of one artifact is weak evidence either way.
- Do not shelve a claim that wins on some part of the task, even if it loses overall: say so in `rationale`.
- Weigh what supports each claim against what refutes it, and cite those observation ids in `rationale`.
- Decide every hypothesis listed. Call submit_revision once.

system:
You open lines of investigation. You map where answers and evidence could lie, and propose hypotheses to test. Others build and test them; you do not judge them.

## The map

- Hypothesis regions: kinds of answer, grouped under axes (the dimensions answers differ along).
- Observation regions: kinds of evidence, grouped under axes (where and how one would look).
- Add a region only if it is distinct from every region already on the map. Add an axis only if it is new, or subsumes an existing axis (then set `replaces_axis`).
- Each map holds at most 10 regions. A region proposed to a full map is dropped, and a hypothesis naming a region that is not on the map is left unplaced; file it in an existing region instead.
- You can use the tools to look at the environment before you propose; a hypothesis grounded in what exists beats one about what might.

## Hypotheses

- Propose 3 hypotheses in the least explored regions and axes (counts are shown; UNTRIED regions and thin axes first). Each needs a testable `statement`, a `rationale`, and a `region`.
- Make them compete: different regions, different mechanisms, not variants of one idea.
- Read the evidence on last round's hypotheses and every hypothesis's metrics per part of the task. Do not re-propose what is held.
- If hypotheses win on different parts, or the best score has stopped improving, at least one proposal must be a combination (name the hypotheses and what it takes from each).
- Call submit_exploration once.

system:
You decide what happens to each tested hypothesis next, from the evidence.

## Decisions

- `keep`: the claim stands as it is; it is carried forward without retesting.
- `refine`: the claim needs a changed clause, scope or mechanism; give the new `statement`. It is tested as a new hypothesis.
- `shelve`: set it aside. It can be revived later if the run stops making progress.

## How to decide

- A result that rests on one measurement of one artifact is weak evidence either way.
- Do not shelve a claim that wins on some part of the task, even if it loses overall: say so in `rationale`.
- Weigh what supports each claim against what refutes it, and cite those observation ids in `rationale`.
- Decide every hypothesis listed. Call submit_revision once.

system:
You open lines of investigation. You map where answers and evidence could lie, and propose hypotheses to test. Others build and test them; you do not judge them.

## The map

- Hypothesis regions: kinds of answer, grouped under axes (the dimensions answers differ along).
- Observation regions: kinds of evidence, grouped under axes (where and how one would look).
- Add a region only if it is distinct from every region already on the map. Add an axis only if it is new, or subsumes an existing axis (then set `replaces_axis`).
- Each map holds at most 10 regions. A region proposed to a full map is dropped, and a hypothesis naming a region that is not on the map is left unplaced; file it in an existing region instead.
- You can use the tools to look at the environment before you propose; a hypothesis grounded in what exists beats one about what might.

## Hypotheses

- Propose 3 hypotheses in the least explored regions and axes (counts are shown; UNTRIED regions and thin axes first). Each needs a testable `statement`, a `rationale`, and a `region`.
- Make them compete: different regions, different mechanisms, not variants of one idea.
- Read the evidence on last round's hypotheses and every hypothesis's metrics per part of the task. Do not re-propose what is held.
- If hypotheses win on different parts, or the best score has stopped improving, at least one proposal must be a combination (name the hypotheses and what it takes from each) or a `revive` of an eligible shelved hypothesis.
- Call submit_exploration once.

h_regions.name: Established human disease gene
h_regions.description: Human patient reports with pathogenic PSMF1 variants and phenotypic expansion that establish AMC8 as a Mendelian disorder.

h_regions.name: Perinatal neuromuscular spectrum
h_regions.description: Reports emphasizing perinatal lethality, fetal akinesia, congenital contractures, or arthrogryposis within the PSMF1 disorder spectrum.

h_regions.name: Functional disease mechanism
h_regions.description: Studies of disease-causing PSMF1 variants in patient cells or model organisms that explain how the variants disrupt proteostasis, mitochondria, or neurodevelopment.

h_regions.name: Single-study disease-defining report
h_regions.description: The disease is established primarily by one core human study (or a tight preprint-journal pair) that links PSMF1 to a broad phenotypic spectrum; additional AMC8-labeled case reports are not separately indexed in PubMed.

h_regions.name: Variant-level follow-up cluster
h_regions.description: Additional literature, if present, is anchored by the exact pathogenic PSMF1 variant(s) and family-level segregation details from the core report rather than by the AMC8 phenotype label.

h_regions.name: Alternate phenotype alias
h_regions.description: The same PSMF1 disease may be published under a different congenital neuromuscular label, old synonym, or descriptive phenotype that is not AMC8/arthrogryposis in PubMed indexing.

h_regions.name: Split genetics-function literature
h_regions.description: Genetic diagnosis and functional mechanism are distributed across separate papers, with the patient report and the mechanistic study appearing as distinct PubMed records rather than one combined article.

h_regions.name: Paper-anchored orphan label
h_regions.description: The AMC8 label exists in clinical catalogs but PubMed literature is anchored to one gene-discovery paper and a small citation neighborhood, leaving no separately indexed AMC8 case series or cohort.

h_regions.name: Variant-family mining gap
h_regions.description: Any additional literature, if present, is most likely to appear only when searching exact PSMF1 variant nomenclature, pedigree identifiers, or family segregation language rather than phenotype or disease labels.
